input.quote: c. the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services.
input.rationale: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose broadly mutual caps, but (i) the floor is $100,000 rather than USD 1,000,000 and is measured on charges "paid" only, not "paid or payable"; (ii) there are no carve-outs for breach of confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or infringement of the other party's IP (only indemnification and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the cap); and (iii) Section 9.1(c)(2) wholly excludes IBM's liability for loss of or damage to Customer's records or data, which is the core risk in a hosting arrangement and is reinforced by the Section 6 statement that Sections 5, 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement. Section 10's mutual consequential-damages exclusion (with its carve-out for Customer's payment obligations) is acceptable. Redline raises the mutual floor to $1,000,000 on fees paid or payable, deletes the data-loss exclusion, and adds one mutual uncapped carve-out sentence.

proposal.summary: Raise mutual cap floor to $1,000,000 on fees paid or payable, delete IBM's exclusion for loss of Customer data, and add mutual uncapped carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have set the mutual cap at the greater of $1,000,000 or the charges paid or payable in the preceding twelve months, and added a mutual carve-out so that confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap. We have also removed the blanket exclusion of liability for loss of or damage to our records and data, which is the principal risk in a hosting engagement; if helpful, we can accept a mutual 12-month fee cap with carve-outs limited to indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

ops.text: The limitations and exclusions in Sections 9.1, 9.2 and 10 do not apply to, and neither party's liability is limited for: (a) breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations; (b) its indemnification obligations; (c) its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud; or (d) its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.
